text:
maya: ran a focused bakeoff today — Mistral3 16B, GPTQ vs AWQ vs int8 naive, on H100 pools. saw weird accuracy swings when we enable Triton + TensorRT-LLM path.

sam: quick summary numbers?

maya: baseline fp16 perf is fine. GPTQ (4-bit) keeps ~0.6% emd loss on our eval set. AWQ profile gives 1.9% delta but much faster. int8/FP8 experiments have mixed results depending on CUDA + driver combo.

jonathan: what driver/kernel versions? Triton, vLLM, TRT-LLM versions?

maya: tested across three stacks:
- vLLM runtime (git: main) on CUDA 11.8, driver 520.x
- Triton server 23.08 w/ TensorRT 8.6 on CUDA 11.8, driver 525.x
- TRT-LLM container (custom) on CUDA 12.1, driver 535.x

chi: sounds like a mismatch. any segfaults or just accuracy noise?

maya: both. two types:
1) determinism/accuracy drift that appears only when serving with Triton + TRT-LLM plugin (requests with batching >1) — small but consistent token-level deviations.
2) intermittent kernel OOM / segfault on CUDA 12.1 + AWQ fused kernels when KV cache grows past ~8k tokens. logs below.

maya: ```
E0312 14:22:11.342 TritonModelInstance: failing request: cuLaunchKernel() -> CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES
Backtrace: trt_llm_plugin.cu:341
context: model:mistral3-16b quant=awq batch=8 seq=2048
```

eva: re: token drift — could be due to FP8 math path + reduced accumulation precision. Did you try forcing deterministic kernels or pinning mm/matmul to fp32 accumulation?

maya: yes. forcing accumulation to fp32 in the runtime removes most of the accuracy gap but throughput drops 20-30%.

sam: is this specific to AWQ, or seen for GPTQ too?

maya: GPTQ is more stable across stacks but still shows tiny deltas with Triton batching enabled. The real outliers are AWQ + TRT-LLM on CUDA 12.1 driver 535 where we hit OOMs.

jonathan: could be allocator or per-stream sync changes in driver 535. We saw a similar symptom last quarter with large KV caches and multi-threaded inference.

chi: any repro steps we can run on a single node?

maya: minimal repro: start TRT-LLM container with `--batching=true --max-batch=8`, load AWQ Mistral3, run perf client with sequence length 2048 and repeated prefix warmups (to fill KV cache). script: 
```bash
python bench_perf.py --model mistral3-awq --batch 8 --seq 2048 --warmups 100 --iters 200
```

maya: observed instability at iteration ~120 consistently on driver 535. on 525 it runs to completion but us shows accuracy drift.

eva: do you have numeric diffs? small example tokens or perplexity change?

maya: paste of eval diffs (trimmed):
```
prompt 452: fp16 -> "...policy."
gptq -> "...policy."
awq-trt -> "...policy ,"  (extra comma)
EM delta: -1.9%
BLEU delta: -2.3%
```

sam: extra comma — likely quantization rounding + softmax numeric differences amplified by beam search. Batching can expose nondeterminism in order of reductions.

jonathan: actionable items:
- chi to reproduce with driver 535 + a debug build of TRT-LLM with extra checks (owner: chi)
- infra to spin up CUDA 11.8 / 525 and CUDA 12.1 / 535 nodes for comparative runs (owner: eva)
- maya to run a small eval where we force fp32 accumulation and compare token-level diffs (owner: maya)

chi: I'll add guarded checks around KV cache pointer reuse and enable CUDA memcheck if needed. plan to instrument with `NVTX` ranges.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-1223: "quant-path instability on TRT-LLM with driver 535" assigned to eng-infra. link: https://redwood.example/t/INF-1223

maya: other note — Triton server sometimes rewrites request order when multiple clients hit it; that changes reduction footprint. Might add a canary config that disables request coalescing.

sam: good idea. also run the same workload on vLLM path without Triton to confirm whether TRT-LLM plugin is necessary trigger.

maya: did that — vLLM + AWQ on 525 had drift but no OOMs. suggests kernel fusion or TRT plugin memory accounting is the main culprit for crashes.

eva: prioritization: block on OOMs (customer-facing instability). chi + infra should give repro and perf delta today. maya + sam to prepare an eval PR that adds fp32-accumulation toggle and automated comparison harness.

jonathan: long-term: consider adding a "safe quant profile" in Optimize that disables FP8 accumulation on production Dedicated pools or forces per-model canaries.

maya: agreed. logging here so we don't lose context. will post short artifacts in the model onboarding repo once repro is nailed. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — keep updates here. :eyes:
